question.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}3e-\frac{1}{2}{(0.99)}^{x} & >-2e \\ -\frac{1}{2}{(0.99)}^{x} & >-5e \\ {(0.99)}^{x} & <10e.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[(0.99)^{x}] & <\operatorname{ln}⁡(10e) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.99) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡(10e)\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.99)$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & >\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(10e)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.99)}\end{aligned}
$$
